mainTopic: Trusting a sinner's food and שחיטה: the חמץ proof, the ברייתא of הכל שוחטין, and רב ענן's proof from יהושפט at אחאב's feast.
overview: The גמרא asks how far we can trust a sinner about food. It first uses a ברייתא about חמץ held by sinners after פסח, which is permitted 'because they exchange' it. From this it proves that even a sinner will not leave permitted food to eat forbidden food. It then tries to support רבא from a ברייתא that says everyone may slaughter, even a ערל and a ישראל משומד. The proof is pushed off: the משומד there is someone who worships idols, following רב ענן in the name of שמואל, who allows eating from such a person's שחיטה. רב ענן's source is that the righteous king יהושפט ate at the feast of the idol-worshipping king אחאב. The גמרא tests this proof step by step. It asks whether יהושפט really ate, and whether he only drank. It then asks who did the slaughtering: עובדיה, the seven thousand, or אחאב's servants. The amud ends with one more possibility, that each king's men slaughtered for their own side, and the answer comes on the next amud.

steps.title: End of the ברייתא: the חמץ is permitted right away because they exchange it
steps.stepSummary: The quoted ברייתא ends by ruling that the sinners' חמץ is permitted immediately after פסח, because they exchange it.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is permitted immediately, because they exchange it.
steps.whatsHappening: We are hearing the end of a ברייתא that the גמרא brought as a proof. It says the חמץ is permitted right after פסח, because the sinners swap their own חמץ for permitted חמץ.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally, חמץ that a Jew owned during פסח is forbidden afterward. The ברייתא permits buying from these sinners right away. Its reason is that they swap their forbidden stock for permitted חמץ belonging to non-Jews.

keyTerms.meaning: They exchange or swap their stock

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new topic. It is the last line of a ברייתא that the גמרא is using as evidence about how sinners behave.

phrases.english: is permitted immediately,
because they exchange it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the ברייתא that the גמרא quoted just before this text.
steps.raayaObject: That a sinner will not leave the permitted to eat the forbidden.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא about חמץ owned by sinners after פסח.

steps.title: Reading the ברייתא as רבי יהודה's view proves a sinner won't choose the forbidden
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא first assumes the ברייתא follows רבי יהודה. In his view this חמץ is forbidden מדאורייתא, yet the sinners still swap it. So a sinner does not leave the permitted to eat the forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: They assumed: whose view is this? It is רבי יהודה's, who says חמץ after פסח is forbidden by Torah law. And it teaches 'because they exchange.' So a person does not leave what is permitted and eat what is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the ברייתא counts as a proof. It assumes the ברייתא follows רבי יהודה, who treats this חמץ as a Torah prohibition.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יהודה, the sinners' own חמץ is forbidden מדאורייתא. Even so, the ברייתא trusts that they swapped it for permitted חמץ. So even a sinner, when permitted food is available, will not go for the forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: They assumed; a first idea that may be questioned later
So we see; this shows that
A person does not leave the permitted and eat the forbidden

steps.whyThisMatters: This principle is the key to the larger discussion. It is why a sinner who sins out of appetite might still be trusted when permitted food is easy to get.

phrases.english: They assumed: whose view is this?
phrases.notes: "They" means the people who brought this ברייתא as a proof. The word signals an assumption the גמרא may question.

phrases.english: It is רבי יהודה's, who says:
חמץ after פסח is forbidden by Torah law,
and it teaches: because they exchange it,
so we see that he does not leave the permitted
and eat the forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: סַבְרוּהָ, הָא מַנִּי? רַבִּי יְהוּדָה הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the general rule out of the ברייתא quoted in step 1.
steps.raayaObject: A sinner does not leave the permitted to eat the forbidden, even for a Torah prohibition.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא's reason 'because they exchange', read according to רבי יהודה.

steps.title: Perhaps the ברייתא follows רבי שמעון, where the ban is only rabbinic
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back. Maybe the ברייתא follows רבי שמעון, for whom this חמץ is only forbidden דרבנן. Being lenient in a rabbinic case would prove nothing about Torah prohibitions.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do you know this? Perhaps it is רבי שמעון's view, who says חמץ after פסח is only rabbinic. When we are lenient, it is in rabbinic matters. In Torah matters we are not lenient!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the proof from step 2. It suggests the ברייתא could follow רבי שמעון instead of רבי יהודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the ban is only דרבנן, the ברייתא's trust in the swap may just be a rabbinic leniency. That would teach nothing about Torah prohibitions, such as forbidden meat. So the proof might not hold.

phrases.english: From where do you know? Perhaps it is רבי שמעון's view,
who says: חמץ after פסח is forbidden only by rabbinic law,
and when we are lenient, it is in rabbinic matters;
in Torah matters we are not lenient!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the assumption in step 2 that the ברייתא follows רבי יהודה.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof from the ברייתא, not the rule itself.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The ברייתא could follow רבי שמעון. Then it only shows a rabbinic leniency, which cannot be applied to Torah prohibitions.

steps.title: Even under רבי שמעון the proof stands, by a קל וחומר
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the ברייתא's wording presents the swap as a certain fact, not a lenient guess. If a sinner won't choose the forbidden even in a rabbinic matter, then surely not in a Torah matter.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let it even be רבי שמעון's view. Does it teach 'because I say they exchanged'? It teaches 'because they exchange,' meaning they certainly exchange. And if in a rabbinic matter he does not leave the permitted to eat the forbidden, then in a Torah matter, all the more so!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends the proof. It points to the exact wording of the ברייתא and then argues with a קל וחומר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Had the ברייתא said 'I say they exchanged,' it would be a lenient guess that fits only a rabbinic ban. Instead it says 'because they exchange,' stating a certain fact about how sinners act. If they avoid the forbidden even when the ban is only rabbinic, they will surely avoid it when the ban is from the Torah.

keyTerms.meaning: And let it even be; granting the other side's point
For I say; wording for a guess or assumption
All the more so; the ending of a קַל וָחוֹמֶר

steps.whatToRemember: The difference between 'because they exchange' (a certain fact) and 'I say they exchanged' (a guess) saves the proof. A sinner does not leave the permitted to eat the forbidden. This holds whether the ban is rabbinic or from the Torah.
steps.confusionAlert: The קל וחומר may seem backward at first. The point is that people care more about Torah bans than rabbinic ones. So if they avoid even a rabbinic ban, they will surely avoid a Torah ban.

phrases.english: And let it even be רבי שמעון's view;
does it teach 'because I say they exchanged'?
phrases.notes: That wording would sound like a guess, the kind of guess we allow only in a rabbinic matter.

phrases.english: It teaches 'because they exchange,'
meaning they certainly exchange.
And if in a rabbinic matter he does not leave the permitted
and eat the forbidden,
in a Torah matter, all the more so!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְתִיהְוֵי נָמֵי רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן, מִי קָתָנֵי ״שֶׁאֲנִי אוֹמֵר הֶחְלִיפוּ״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the rejection in step 3 and keeps the proof from step 2 standing.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Precise reading of the wording plus a קל וחומר
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Under רבי שמעון, the ברייתא is only a rabbinic leniency that cannot teach about Torah law.
steps.terutzMaskana: The wording 'because they exchange' states a certain fact about how sinners behave. That fact applies all the more so to Torah prohibitions.

steps.title: A ברייתא That Might Support רבא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that a ברייתא listing everyone who may slaughter supports רבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let us say this supports him: Everyone may slaughter, even a כותי, even an uncircumcised man, and even a Jewish sinner.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that seems to back up רבא. It is setting up a proof that will be worked out in the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא lets three surprising people slaughter: a כותי, a ערל, and a ישראל משומד. If the משומד here is someone who eats נבלות, that would match רבא's ruling that such a sinner's שחיטה can be relied on.

keyTerms.meaning: Let us say this supports him (a suggested proof)
A Jew who regularly breaks a מצוה

phrases.english: Let us say this supports him:
phrases.notes: 'Him' is רבא, whose ruling about a sinner who eats נבלות the גמרא has been discussing.

phrases.english: Everyone may slaughter,
and even a Samaritan,
and even an uncircumcised man,
and even a Jewish transgressor.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a new source to support רבא's position after the previous proof was settled.
steps.raayaObject: רבא's ruling that a sinner who eats נבלות for convenience may be relied on for שחיטה

steps.title: Who Is the Uncircumcised Man?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what kind of ערל the ברייתא means, and rules out a man whose brothers died from מילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: This uncircumcised man, what is the case? If he is one whose brothers died from circumcision, he is a perfectly fine Jew!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks which ערל the ברייתא is talking about. It rejects the first option because that man isn't a sinner at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A man whose brothers died from מילה is allowed to stay uncircumcised, so he is a fully proper Jew. Of course he may slaughter, and the ברייתא would not need to say 'even' about him.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the case? How do we picture it?
His brothers died because of circumcision

phrases.english: This uncircumcised man, what is the case?
If you say his brothers died because of circumcision,
he is a perfectly fine Jew!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts examining the ברייתא's cases, which the proof will build on.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What kind of ערל does the ברייתא mean?

steps.title: He Refuses Circumcision
steps.stepSummary: The ערל must be a sinner who refuses מילה, and the תנא holds that sinning in one area doesn't make him a sinner for the whole Torah.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is obvious he is a sinner about staying uncircumcised, and the תנא holds that a sinner in one matter is not a sinner for the whole Torah.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא concludes that the ערל is someone who refuses to have a ברית מילה, and that he may still slaughter.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Sinning in one מצוה does not make him untrustworthy for every מצוה. So a man who refuses מילה can still be trusted to slaughter properly.

keyTerms.meaning: A sinner who refuses to be circumcised
A sinner in one specific matter

phrases.english: Rather, it is obvious he is a transgressor about staying uncircumcised,
and he holds
a transgressor in one matter

phrases.aramaic: לָא הָוֵי מְשׁוּמָּד לְכׇל הַתּוֹרָה כּוּלָּהּ.
phrases.english: is not a transgressor for the entire Torah.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 6.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The ערל refuses מילה, and a sinner in one matter isn't a sinner for the whole Torah.

steps.title: The Last Clause Must Mean a Sinner With נבלות
steps.stepSummary: Since a sinner in another matter is already covered by the ערל, the ישראל משומד must be a sinner in eating נבלות, which matches רבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Look at the last clause: 'even a Jewish sinner.' What is the case? If he sins in some other matter, that is the same as the ערל. So isn't he a sinner in that very matter, like רבא?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the proof. The משומד at the end of the ברייתא must be someone who eats נבלות, and he may still slaughter, just like רבא says.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ערל already taught that a sinner in some other area may slaughter. So the extra case of a משומד must teach something new: even someone who sins in the very matter of נבלות may slaughter.

keyTerms.meaning: A sinner in some other matter
A sinner in that very matter (here: eating נבלות)

phrases.english: Say the last clause:
and even a Jewish transgressor.
This transgressor, what is the case?
If he is a transgressor in another matter,
that is the same as the transgressor about staying uncircumcised.
Rather, is it not a transgressor in that very matter,
phrases.notes: 'That very matter' means eating meat that wasn't properly slaughtered, the thing he is now slaughtering.

phrases.english: and this follows רבא?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the conclusion about the ערל to work out who the משומד must be.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The סיפא of the ברייתא, which would otherwise repeat the ערל case

steps.title: A Sinner in That Very Matter Cannot Slaughter
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof: a sinner who eats נבלות is not included, because he treats it as permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, really I will tell you: a sinner in that very matter is not included. Why? Since he is used to it, it seems permitted to him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the proof. The ברייתא's משומד cannot be someone who eats נבלות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone who regularly eats נבלות has gotten so used to it that it feels permitted to him. So we can't simply trust him to slaughter properly, and the ברייתא's 'everyone may slaughter' can't include him.

keyTerms.meaning: Really, I will tell you (the case is different than you thought)
He has trampled on it, meaning he has gotten used to doing it
It seems to him like something permitted

steps.confusionAlert: This step does not reject רבא's ruling itself. It only shows that this ברייתא is not a proof for him.

phrases.english: No, really I will tell you:
a transgressor in that very matter, no.
phrases.notes: He means the ברייתא is not talking about him.

phrases.english: What is the reason?
Since he has trampled on it,
phrases.notes: Literally 'trampled.' He does it so often that it feels normal to him.

phrases.english: it seems to him like something permitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the reading of the ברייתא given in step 8.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proof from the ברייתא, not רבא's ruling itself.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed the ברייתא includes a sinner in that very matter, but such a sinner treats it as permitted, so the ברייתא can't mean him.

steps.title: The ברייתא Means an Idol Worshipper
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא's משומד is a משומד לעבודה זרה, following רב ענן in the name of שמואל.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it means a sinner in idol worship, like רב ענן, who said in the name of שמואל: a Jew who is a sinner in idol worship, we may eat from his slaughtering.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains what the ברייתא really means: a Jew who worships idols.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This solves the problem from step 8. A sinner in עבודה זרה is not just 'the same as the ערל,' because עבודה זרה is so severe. So the ברייתא needed to teach that even he may slaughter, and this matches רב ענן.

keyTerms.meaning: It is permitted to eat from his slaughtering

steps.whatToRemember: The proof for רבא falls away. The ברייתא's ישראל משומד is understood as an idol worshipper, whose שחיטה רב ענן permits.

phrases.english: Rather, it means a transgressor in idol worship,
and this follows רב ענן,
for רב ענן said in the name of שמואל:
a Jew who is a transgressor in idol worship,
it is permitted to eat from his slaughtering.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the rejection by giving another way to read the ברייתא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Re-reading the case in the ברייתא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משומד in the ברייתא is a sinner who eats נבלות, supporting רבא.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משומד in the ברייתא is an idol worshipper, following רב ענן.

steps.title: רב ענן's Ruling Itself
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא turns to study רב ענן's statement directly: we may eat from the שחיטה of a משומד לעבודה זרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The matter itself: רב ענן said in the name of שמואל: a Jew who is a sinner in idol worship, we may eat from his slaughtering.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now looks at רב ענן's statement on its own. It is setting up his source, which comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now רב ענן was quoted only to explain the ברייתא. 'גופא' means the גמרא will study the statement itself, starting with the reason he gives.

keyTerms.meaning: The matter itself: now we study a statement that was quoted earlier

phrases.english: The matter itself:
רב ענן said in the name of שמואל:
a Jew who is a transgressor in idol worship,
it is permitted to eat from his slaughtering,

steps.triggerLanguage: גּוּפָא, אָמַר רַב עָנָן אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Picks up the statement quoted in step 10 for its own discussion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: We may eat from the שחיטה of a Jew who worships idols.

steps.title: Proof From יהושפט at אחאב's Feast
steps.stepSummary: רב ענן's source: יהושפט, a righteous king, ate at the feast of אחאב, an idol worshipper who slaughtered animals for him.
steps.simpleTranslation: For we found that יהושפט king of יהודה benefited from אחאב's feast, as it says: 'And אחאב slaughtered for him sheep and cattle in abundance, and for the people with him, and enticed him to go up to רמות גלעד.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב ענן proves his ruling from a פסוק. יהושפט ate meat that אחאב slaughtered.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אחאב worshipped idols, yet the righteous יהושפט ate from the animals אחאב slaughtered. This shows that a משומד לעבודה זרה's שחיטה is permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: For so we have found (an earlier example)

phrases.english: for so we found with Jehoshaphat king of Judah,
who benefited from Ahab's feast,
as it is said:
"And Ahab slaughtered for him sheep and cattle in abundance,
and for the people who were with him,
and he enticed him to go up to Ramoth Gilead."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for the ruling stated in step 11.
steps.raayaObject: רב ענן's ruling that a משומד לעבודה זרה's שחיטה is permitted
steps.raayaSupportSource: דברי הימים ב 18:2: יהושפט ate from the animals אחאב slaughtered

steps.title: Maybe אחאב slaughtered but יהושפט did not eat
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב ענן's proof: the פסוק says אחאב slaughtered animals, but maybe יהושפט never ate the meat.
steps.simpleTranslation: But perhaps he slaughtered, yet he did not eat!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the proof from step 12. It points out that the פסוק only tells us אחאב slaughtered, not that יהושפט ate.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב ענן's proof works only if יהושפט actually ate meat from אחאב's שחיטה. If יהושפט just attended without eating, the story tells us nothing about whether that meat is permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: But perhaps (introduces another way to read the case that weakens a proof)

phrases.english: But perhaps he [אחאב] slaughtered,
but he [יהושפט] did not eat!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְדִלְמָא מִיזְבָּח זְבַח, מֵיכַל לָא אֲכַל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the proof brought in step 12.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב ענן's proof from יהושפט at אחאב's feast
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק mentions only slaughtering, not eating, so the proof is incomplete.

steps.title: The word 'he enticed him' shows that יהושפט ate
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק says אחאב 'enticed' יהושפט, and enticing implies food, so יהושפט ate.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And he enticed him' is written.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the פסוק itself says אחאב enticed יהושפט. That suggests he won him over with a meal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof now leans on one word, וַיְסִיתֵהוּ. The idea is that 'enticing' someone means winning him over with food, so יהושפט must have eaten.

keyTerms.meaning: And he enticed him (from the פסוק about אחאב and יהושפט)

phrases.english: "And he enticed him" is written,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 13.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Textual reading: a word in the פסוק implies eating
steps.terutzHavaAmina: יהושפט may have attended without eating.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'Enticed' implies a meal, so he ate.

steps.title: Maybe the enticing was only with words
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: maybe אחאב enticed יהושפט with words, not with food.
steps.simpleTranslation: But perhaps with words.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on step 14. Maybe 'enticing' here just means persuading with talk.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If enticing can be done by talking, the word וַיְסִיתֵהוּ no longer proves that יהושפט ate. The proof would fall apart again.

phrases.english: But perhaps [he enticed him] with words,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reading in step 14.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading that וַיְסִיתֵהוּ implies food
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Enticing might be verbal, so it does not prove that יהושפט ate.

steps.title: Enticing is not done with words
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the term הסתה does not refer to words alone.
steps.simpleTranslation: There is no enticement with words.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא states a rule: real 'enticing' is not done only with words.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This sets the meaning of the word הסתה as winning someone over with something tangible like food. With this rule in place, the proof from וַיְסִיתֵהוּ stands again.

keyTerms.meaning: Enticement is not done with words alone

phrases.english: There is no enticement with words.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 15.
steps.terutzMaskana: הסתה means enticing with food, not with words.

steps.title: The מסית seems to entice with words
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges from the פסוק of the מסית, who seems to entice someone to idolatry by talking.
steps.simpleTranslation: And is there not? But it is written: 'If your brother entices you'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions the rule from step 16. The פסוק about a מסית, someone who lures others to idolatry, seems to describe enticing with words.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The full פסוק continues 'saying: let us go and serve other gods,' which sounds like a speech. If that counts as הסתה, then enticing can be done with words.

keyTerms.meaning: But is it not written? (introduces a פסוק that contradicts a claim)
Entices you (the מֵסִית who lures others to idolatry)

phrases.english: And is there not [enticement with words]?
But is it not written: "If your brother entices you"!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the rule stated in step 16.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The מסית in the תורה seems to entice by talking.

steps.title: The מסית also entices with food and drink
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the מסית also wins people over with eating and drinking.
steps.simpleTranslation: With eating and with drinking.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the מסית too uses food and drink to lure people. So the rule still holds.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words of the מסית come along with a meal that wins the person over. So the פסוק of the מסית does not show enticing with words alone.

phrases.english: [There too it is] with eating and with drinking.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 17.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The מסית entices only by talking.
steps.terutzMaskana: The מסית also entices with food and drink.

steps.title: שטן 'enticed' ה׳ without food
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges from איוב, where ה׳ says שטן enticed Him, which obviously had nothing to do with food.
steps.simpleTranslation: But it is written: 'And you enticed Me against him, to destroy him for nothing'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another פסוק. In איוב‎, ה׳ tells שטן 'you enticed Me,' and that clearly could not be with food or drink.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a strong counter-example. The same word for enticing is used where no meal is possible, so maybe the word does not require food after all.

keyTerms.meaning: And you enticed Me against him
To destroy him for no reason

phrases.english: But is it not written:
"And you enticed Me against him, to destroy him for nothing"!
phrases.notes: איוב 2:3. ה׳ is speaking to שטן about איוב.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second challenge to the rule אין הסתה בדברים.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that הסתה involves food
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: ה׳ was 'enticed' with no food or drink at all.

steps.title: Enticing toward ה׳ is different
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the word works differently when speaking about ה׳.
steps.simpleTranslation: Above is different.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that when the פסוק speaks about ה׳, the word 'enticed' is used in a different way. For people, enticing still means with food.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Language used about ה׳ is not meant literally, so it does not set the meaning for human cases. The rule stands, and so does the proof that יהושפט ate.

phrases.english: [Enticement toward the One] above is different.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 19 and closes the discussion about the meaning of הסתה.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The word הסתה never requires food.
steps.terutzMaskana: With people, הסתה means with food; toward ה׳ it is used differently.
steps.whatToRemember: The word וַיְסִיתֵהוּ shows that יהושפט was won over with a meal, because enticing people means with food and drink.

steps.title: Maybe יהושפט only drank
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא raises a new challenge: maybe יהושפט only drank at the feast and did not eat the meat.
steps.simpleTranslation: But perhaps he drank a drink, but he did not eat?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא accepts that יהושפט was won over with a feast. But it asks whether he maybe only drank there.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Enticing can be done with food or drink. If יהושפט only drank, there is still no proof that he ate meat slaughtered by אחאב.

phrases.english: But perhaps he drank a drink,
but he did not eat?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְדִלְמָא מִשְׁתָּא אִשְׁתִּי, מֵיכַל לָא אֲכַל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the meaning of הסתה is settled, a new gap in the proof is raised.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Enticing with drink alone fits the פסוק, so eating meat is not proven.

steps.title: Eating and drinking should follow the same rule
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא argues: if drinking was allowed because an idol worshipper is not treated as rejecting the whole תורה, the same should be true of eating.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is different about drinking? That we say a משומד לעבודה זרה is not a משומד for the whole תורה. Eating too: a משומד לעבודה זרה is not a משומד for the whole תורה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that drinking and eating should not be different. Whatever reason allowed the drinking should allow the eating too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The only reason יהושפט could drink אחאב's wine would be that a משומד לעבודה זרה is not treated as rejecting the whole תורה. That same reason would also allow eating his שחיטה, so the proof for רב ענן still works.

keyTerms.meaning: Someone treated as rejecting the entire תורה

phrases.english: What is different about drinking?
That we say:
phrases.notes: He means: the only reason drinking would be allowed is the rule that follows.

phrases.english: a transgressor regarding idol worship

phrases.aramaic: לָא הָוֵי מְשׁוּמָּד לְכׇל הַתּוֹרָה כּוּלָּהּ,
phrases.english: is not a transgressor regarding the entire Torah.
Eating too:
a transgressor regarding idol worship

phrases.aramaic: לָא הָוֵי מְשׁוּמָּד לְכׇל הַתּוֹרָה כּוּלָּהּ.
phrases.english: is not a transgressor regarding the entire Torah.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 21 by comparing drinking to eating.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Comparison: the same reasoning applies to both
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Maybe יהושפט only drank, which proves nothing about meat.
steps.terutzMaskana: Drinking could only be allowed for a reason that would allow eating too.
steps.confusionAlert: This step does not yet give the final answer. The very next line rejects this comparison.

steps.title: The drinking was allowed for a different reason
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the comparison: drinking was allowed because non-Jewish wine was not yet forbidden, so eating may still be forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is this so? Drinking is their plain wine, and the wine of non-Jews was not yet forbidden. But eating, I will tell you: a משומד לעבודה זרה is a משומד for the whole תורה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects step 22. Drinking was allowed for a separate reason: in those days, ordinary non-Jewish wine was not forbidden yet.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Drinking was allowed because אחאב's wine counted like any ordinary non-Jewish wine, and the ban on that wine had not been made yet. So drinking tells us nothing about meat. A משומד לעבודה זרה might still be treated as rejecting the whole תורה, which would make his שחיטה forbidden, and the proof for רב ענן is weakened again.

keyTerms.meaning: How can you compare? (rejects a comparison)
Their ordinary wine (wine of non-Jews with no known idol use)

phrases.english: How can you compare?
Drinking: it is their ordinary wine,

phrases.aramaic: וַעֲדַיִין לֹא נֶאֱסַר יֵינָן שֶׁל גּוֹיִם,
phrases.english: and the wine of non-Jews had not yet been forbidden.
But eating, I will say to you:
a transgressor regarding idol worship
is a transgressor regarding the entire Torah.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכִי הַשְׁתָּא? שְׁתִיָּה – סְתָם יֵינָן הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the comparison made in step 22, which brings back the challenge of step 21.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The comparison between drinking and eating
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Drinking was allowed for a separate reason: ordinary non-Jewish wine was not yet forbidden. So it shows nothing about a משומד לעבודה זרה's meat.
steps.whyThisMatters: The proof for רב ענן is shaky again, since יהושפט may have only drunk wine, which was allowed then for a separate reason.

steps.title: A king does not drink without eating
steps.stepSummary: The first answer: יהושפט surely ate, because a king does not drink without eating.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you want, say this: it is not normal for a king to drink without eating.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the doubt from the last step, that maybe יהושפט only drank. It says a king would not drink at a feast without also eating.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 23 left open the idea that יהושפט only drank and never touched the meat. This answer closes that door using how kings normally behave. If he drank, he also ate, so he ate the slaughtered meat.

keyTerms.meaning: If you want, say this (introduces one possible answer out of several)

phrases.english: If you wish, say:
it is not the way of a king
to drink without eating.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the open doubt from steps 21 and 23 that יהושפט may only have drunk.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Maybe יהושפט drank but did not eat the meat.
steps.terutzMaskana: A king does not drink without eating, so he certainly ate.

steps.title: The פסוק shows he was won over through slaughtered meat
steps.stepSummary: The second answer: the פסוק links the slaughtering to how אחאב persuaded יהושפט, so the meat was eaten.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or if you want, say this: it is written "And he slaughtered... and enticed him." How did he entice him? With the slaughtering.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second answer, this time from the פסוק itself. אחאב won יהושפט over by means of the slaughtered meat.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק puts "he slaughtered" right next to "he enticed him." The גמרא reads this as saying the slaughtered meat was the tool of persuasion. That only works if יהושפט actually ate it.

phrases.english: And if you wish, say:
"And he slaughtered... and enticed him" is written,
phrases.notes: דברי הימים ב 18:2. אחאב slaughtered sheep and cattle for יהושפט.

phrases.english: With what did he entice him? With slaughter.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second, separate answer to the same doubt, this time based on the פסוק.
steps.raayaObject: That יהושפט ate the slaughtered meat.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The פסוק joins "he slaughtered" with "he enticed him," so the meat was the way he was persuaded.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reading of the פסוק: the slaughter was the means of enticement
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Maybe יהושפט only drank and did not eat the slaughtered meat.
steps.terutzMaskana: The פסוק links וַיִּזְבַּח to וַיְסִיתֵהוּ, so he was enticed with the slaughtered meat, which means he ate it.

steps.title: Maybe the righteous עובדיה did the slaughtering
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that עובדיה, a righteous man in אחאב's house, may have slaughtered the animals.
steps.simpleTranslation: But maybe עובדיה slaughtered?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a new doubt about who did the slaughtering. If a righteous person like עובדיה slaughtered, the proof falls apart.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now it is clear that יהושפט ate the meat. But the proof only works if idol worshippers slaughtered it. עובדיה served in אחאב's household and feared ה׳, so maybe the meat came from him.

phrases.english: And perhaps Obadiah slaughtered?
phrases.notes: עובדיה was in charge of אחאב's household and was a righteous man.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts that he ate, and now questions who slaughtered.
steps.kashyaTarget: The assumption that idol worshippers slaughtered the meat.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A righteous slaughterer would make the meat kosher for an ordinary reason, so it proves nothing.

steps.title: One man could not slaughter so many animals
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק says "in abundance," which is far too much for עובדיה to slaughter by himself.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is written "in abundance"; עובדיה could not have managed it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the עובדיה idea. The פסוק says there were very many animals, more than one person could slaughter.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same פסוק says אחאב slaughtered "in abundance." One man alone could not handle that much. So others must have slaughtered too.

phrases.english: "In abundance" is written,
Obadiah would not have managed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the suggestion of step 26.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Practical impossibility shown from the פסוק
steps.terutzMaskana: There were too many animals for one person.

steps.title: Maybe the seven thousand righteous people slaughtered
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that the seven thousand people who never bowed to בעל did the slaughtering.
steps.simpleTranslation: But maybe the seven thousand slaughtered, as it is written: "And I will leave in ישראל seven thousand, all the knees that did not bow to בעל..."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא suggests another group of righteous slaughterers. There were seven thousand people who never served בעל, and there were enough of them to slaughter a lot.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This answers the problem from step 27: one man was not enough, but seven thousand people would be plenty. If they slaughtered, the meat came from righteous hands, and the proof is gone again.

phrases.english: And perhaps the seven thousand slaughtered,
as it is written: "And I will leave in Israel seven thousand,
all the knees that did not bow
to Baal, etc."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gets around step 27's answer by offering a large group of righteous people.
steps.kashyaTarget: The assumption that idol worshippers slaughtered.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A large group of righteous people could have handled the large amount of slaughtering.

steps.title: The seven thousand were in hiding
steps.stepSummary: The seven thousand were hiding from איזבל, so they were not at the palace slaughtering.
steps.simpleTranslation: They were hiding from איזבל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the seven thousand idea. Those righteous people were hiding from איזבל, so they would not be working at אחאב's feast.
steps.deeperAnalysis: איזבל, אחאב's wife, went after people who stayed loyal to ה׳. People in hiding would not show up at the king's palace to slaughter animals.

phrases.english: They were hiding from Jezebel.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the suggestion of step 28.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The seven thousand righteous people slaughtered.
steps.terutzMaskana: They were in hiding and could not have been there.

steps.title: Maybe אחאב's own servants were good people
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that אחאב's servants were decent people who did not serve idols, and they slaughtered.
steps.simpleTranslation: But maybe אחאב's men were upstanding people?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries one last option. Maybe אחאב served idols, but his staff did not, and they did the slaughtering.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Servants solve both earlier problems. There were many of them, and they were right there in the palace. If they were not idol worshippers, the proof would fall apart.

phrases.english: And perhaps the men of Ahab were upstanding?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third possible set of slaughterers, after עובדיה and the seven thousand were ruled out.
steps.kashyaTarget: The assumption that idol worshippers slaughtered.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The servants were many and present, and might have been righteous.

steps.title: A wicked ruler has wicked servants
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the idea using a פסוק: when a ruler listens to falsehood, all his servants are wicked.
steps.simpleTranslation: Don't even think it, as it is written: "A ruler who listens to false words, all his servants are wicked."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא firmly rejects the idea that אחאב's servants were good. A פסוק in משלי teaches that a wicked ruler's servants are wicked too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אחאב served idols, so by the rule in the פסוק his servants did as well. With עובדיה, the seven thousand, and the servants all ruled out, it seems the slaughterers were idol worshippers. The next steps raise new possibilities about who ate which meat.

keyTerms.meaning: Don't even think it; that idea cannot be right

steps.whatToRemember: So far, every other possible slaughterer has been ruled out: עובדיה was only one man, the seven thousand were hiding, and אחאב's servants were wicked like him. The גמרא will still test whether יהושפט himself ate that meat.

phrases.english: It should not enter your mind,
as it is written: "A ruler who listens to words of falsehood,
all his servants are wicked."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the suggestion of step 30 and completes the ruling-out of righteous slaughterers.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: אחאב's servants were decent and they slaughtered.
steps.terutzMaskana: A wicked ruler's servants are wicked, so idol worshippers did the slaughtering.

steps.title: Maybe יהושפט's men were not careful either
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that יהושפט's servants were also not upstanding. They ate what אחאב's men slaughtered, and only יהושפט himself ate what עובדיה slaughtered.
steps.simpleTranslation: Perhaps יהושפט's men were also not upstanding people. Then what אחאב's men slaughtered, יהושפט's men ate, and what עובדיה slaughtered, יהושפט ate.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a new way out. Maybe only יהושפט himself needed kosher meat, and עובדיה could slaughter enough for one person.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 27 rejected עובדיה as the only slaughterer because the meat was "in abundance." This suggestion gets around that problem. If יהושפט's servants did not care, עובדיה only had to slaughter for יהושפט himself, and the huge amount of meat came from אחאב's men.

phrases.english: And perhaps the men of יהושפט
also were not upstanding,
phrases.notes: "Also" means like אחאב's servants, who were just called wicked in step 31.

phrases.english: what the men of אחאב slaughtered,
the men of יהושפט ate,
and what עובדיה slaughtered, יהושפט ate.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְדִלְמָא גַּבְרֵי דִּיהוֹשָׁפָט נָמֵי לָא הֲווֹ מְעַלּוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After step 31 showed that אחאב's servants were wicked, this step suggests that יהושפט's servants were not careful either.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that יהושפט must have eaten meat slaughtered by idol-servers
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If only יהושפט needed kosher meat, עובדיה alone could have supplied it. The large amount of meat could then have gone to יהושפט's careless servants.

steps.title: A righteous king has righteous servants
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the idea. The פסוק teaches that a ruler who listens to lies has wicked servants, so a ruler who follows truth, like יהושפט, has righteous servants.
steps.simpleTranslation: Don't think that. The פסוק says, "A ruler who listens to falsehood, all his servants are wicked." That means a ruler who listens to truth has righteous servants.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back the suggestion from step 32. יהושפט was a righteous king, so his servants were righteous too, and they would not eat meat slaughtered by idol-servers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 31 used this same פסוק to show that אחאב's servants were wicked. Now the גמרא reads the opposite side of the פסוק: if a false ruler has wicked servants, then a truthful ruler has righteous ones. So יהושפט's men also needed kosher meat, and עובדיה alone still could not have slaughtered enough.
steps.confusionAlert: This is the same פסוק as step 31, but it is used in the opposite direction. There it showed that אחאב's men were wicked. Here, by inference, it shows that יהושפט's men were righteous.

phrases.english: That should not enter your mind,
since it says, "A ruler who listens to matters of falsehood,"
"all his servants are wicked,"
this implies that if he listens to matters of truth,
his servants are righteous.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the suggestion of step 32 by reading the other side of the פסוק from step 31.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Inference from the opposite side of a פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: יהושפט's servants might have been careless, so only יהושפט needed עובדיה's meat.
steps.terutzMaskana: A truthful king has righteous servants, so יהושפט's men also needed properly slaughtered meat.

steps.title: Maybe each king's men slaughtered for their own side
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests a new setup. אחאב's men slaughtered for אחאב and his people, and יהושפט's own righteous men slaughtered for יהושפט and his people.
steps.simpleTranslation: Perhaps what אחאב's men slaughtered, אחאב and his men ate. And what יהושפט's men slaughtered, יהושפט and his men ate.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries one more way out. Maybe the two sides kept their meat separate, and יהושפט's side only ate what his own righteous servants slaughtered. The answer comes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 33 established that יהושפט's servants were righteous. The גמרא now turns this into a possible solution: those righteous servants could have done the slaughtering themselves. If so, the story is no proof that יהושפט ate meat slaughtered by idol-servers.

phrases.english: And perhaps what the men of אחאב slaughtered,
אחאב and his men ate,
and what the men of יהושפט slaughtered,
יהושפט and his men ate?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְדִלְמָא זְבוּח גַּבְרֵי דְּאַחְאָב אֲכַל אַחְאָב וְגַבְרֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on step 33's conclusion that יהושפט's men were righteous and suggests that they did their own slaughtering.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that יהושפט ate meat slaughtered by אחאב's idol-serving servants
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If יהושפט's righteous servants slaughtered for their own side, there was no need for יהושפט to eat from אחאב's men at all.
